items.prompt: What is simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)?
items.answer: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is a technique that simultaneously creates and updates a map of a real environment while localizing positions within it, enabling real-time, drift-free tracking of unknown environments.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Virtual environment is a non-real, computer-generated graphical representation of a real or imaginary world, populated with artificial objects, that is experienced through computer-generated sensory stimuli.

A virtual reality system is a system that presents a computer-generated artificial environment, provides computer-generated sensory stimuli for an immersive experience, and lets the user's actions partially determine what happens in it.

A head-mounted display (HMD) is a wearable, mobile visual display that integrates electronic, optical, mechanical, and audio components and uses one or two small screens directly in front of the user's eyes to place images for monoscopic or stereoscopic viewing. It can be non-see-through, optical see-through, or video see-through.

Cybersickness (CS) is a condition primarily relevant to virtual reality that may be caused by multiple internal and external factors and in which a user may experience symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, headache, or disorientation.

questions.question: In a VR or AR system, why does virtual reality software drive the hardware rather than just operating it?
options: To make it store the developer's high-level application descriptions
To make it collect raw sensor data from the user's movements
To make it build a model of the surrounding physical environment
To make it generate appropriate stimuli for the user's sense organs
questions.explanation: The purpose of driving VR or AR hardware is to make the hardware produce stimuli that are received in a way that stimulates the user's senses. Collecting movement data, modeling the surrounding environment, or storing developer descriptions are not the sensory output purpose of the software.

data.text: VR software has a specific purpose with VR or AR hardware. It is not just about operating the devices. By making the hardware produce appropriate sensory stimuli, it enables human sense organs to receive a virtual reality experience.
points: VR software does not merely drive VR or AR hardware; it creates sensory stimuli for a VR experience.

questions.question: Between which pair in a VR system do tracking and stimulation occur?
options: The user and the VR hardware
The VR hardware and the surrounding physical world
The user and the surrounding physical world
The VR engine and the software-and-database component
questions.explanation: Tracking and stimulation form the two-way exchange between the user and the VR hardware. The surrounding physical world and the software components are not the pair described for that exchange.

questions.question: What is the role of output devices in the data flow between a user and VR hardware?
options: To generate stimuli that suitably affect the sense organs
To generate data that the VR system processes
To generate a stored copy of the virtual environment
To generate tracking data about the user's movements
questions.explanation: Output devices receive processed data and create stimuli for the user's sense organs. Input devices are what generate user data, and output devices are not described as tracking or storing the environment.

questions.question: Which part of the VR data flow is responsible for making output-device stimuli suitably stimulate the user's sense organs?
options: Interaction design and modeling
Perceptual design and modeling
Virtual environment modeling and object placement
Software processing and data generation
questions.explanation: Perceptual design and modeling ensure that output-device stimuli suitably stimulate the sense organs. Interaction design concerns the user's use of input devices, while software processing handles input and output data.

data.text: A virtual reality system links the user and virtual reality hardware through bidirectional data flow, with tracking and stimulation moving information in both directions. Input data is sent to the virtual reality system, and processed output data is sent to output devices that stimulate the user's sense organs. This flow requires interaction design, perceptual design, and software, and the software side is represented by a virtual reality engine and a software-and-database component.
points: In a virtual reality system, bidirectional data flow between the user and hardware includes tracking and stimulation.
The virtual reality system processes input data and returns output data that stimulate the user's sense organs.
The virtual reality data flow needs proper interaction design and modeling, perceptual design and modeling, and software.
The software part of the virtual reality data-flow diagram is the virtual reality engine and a software-and-database component.

activities.title: Order the stages of data flow in a VR system

items.title: Order the stages of data flow in a VR system
steps: Data is produced by the user operating input devices
The produced data is sent to the VR system
The data is processed by the VR system
The processed data is sent to output devices
Stimuli for the user's sense organs are generated by output devices

questions.question: Which three activities are central to creating a virtual reality experience?
options: head tracking, stereoscopic output rendering, and interaction incorporation
environment modeling, visual display rendering, and interaction incorporation
texture mapping, stereoscopic output rendering, and interaction incorporation
environment modeling, stereoscopic output rendering, and interaction incorporation
questions.explanation: Creating a VR experience involves building the environment, rendering the stereoscopic output view, and incorporating interactions that use tracking hardware. Head tracking is part of interaction support, texture mapping is one possible world-building method, and visual display rendering is narrower than the stereoscopic output activity.

questions.question: Why is the term rendering used in a broad sense in VR software?
options: because it covers output for senses other than sight
because it refers to tracking the user's head position
because it describes the environment modeling step before output
because it converts a recorded physical world into a synthetic one
questions.explanation: In VR, rendering is not limited to visual display; it can include generating output for other senses. Environment modeling, head tracking, and converting recorded worlds are separate concerns.

questions.question: What may be required in practical VR development that is not part of the ideal high-level support model?
options: using a game engine for lowest-level device driver operations
using a platform SDK for highest-level application design
implementing much functionality from scratch
providing high-level descriptions that determine low-level details
questions.explanation: Practical VR development may require developers to build much functionality from scratch, whereas the ideal model lets high-level descriptions determine low-level details. SDKs handle lowest-level platform operations, not highest-level application design, and game engines act as middleware rather than low-level drivers.

questions.question: What is a main limitation of using a standard game engine as VR middleware?
options: it can be cumbersome for ideas outside standard video games and reduce flexibility
it can avoid the initial effort of adopting game-engine patterns
it can replace the need to understand the SDK for device drivers and display output
it can remove the need for interaction design in original applications
questions.explanation: A game engine can save early effort, but a non-VR engine may be awkward for non-standard ideas and less flexible. It does not remove the need to understand platform SDKs, interaction design, or the initial effort that adopting the engine can reduce.

data.text: Creating a VR application involves three activities: modeling the virtual environment, producing the output view in a broad sense, and adding tracking-based interactions. VR software should support these activities, ideally by letting developers work from high-level descriptions and middleware while also allowing original from-scratch functions. In practice, developers may build substantial parts themselves, rely on a platform-dependent SDK for lowest-level operations, and adopt a game engine as middleware, accepting effort savings in exchange for possible inflexibility.
points: Creating a VR experience involves environment modeling, stereoscopic output rendering in a broad sense, and interactions.
Ideally, VR software supports environment modeling, rendering, and interactions through high-level descriptions, middleware, and from-scratch design.
In practice, VR developers may build from scratch and must understand a platform-dependent SDK for lowest-level operations.
A game engine can be VR middleware, but can be cumbersome and less flexible for ideas outside standard video games.

questions.question: In the virtual world generator abstraction, what is treated as a black box?
options: a real-world recording system
the whole VR software system
a visual-output display system
a head-tracker input system
questions.explanation: The virtual world generator abstraction treats the entire VR software system as a black box, so its internal operation is not considered. A head tracker, renderer, or recorded-world component is only one part that may interact with that abstraction.

questions.question: What does a head tracker estimate?
options: hand position and orientation
eye distance and focus
body height and weight
position and orientation
questions.explanation: A head tracker estimates the user's head position and orientation. It does not provide hand tracking, body dimensions, or eye-focus data in this abstraction.

questions.question: Which two operations in the virtual world generator preserve the relationship between user actions and what the display shows?
options: defining triangular meshes and maintaining surface properties
capturing physical worlds and applying SLAM techniques
converting input to output and synchronizing output devices
mapping camera images onto objects and applying textures
questions.explanation: Converting input into output and synchronizing output devices with input data are the two operations that keep the display tied to user input. Defining meshes, capturing worlds, or mapping textures create world content rather than maintain that relationship.

questions.question: How can a recorded physical world be made realistic for a virtual world?
options: by camera-image mapping and synthetic-object texturing
by input-event queuing and systematic event processing
by camera capture and SLAM or computer-vision techniques
by triangular-mesh definition and surface-property maintenance
questions.explanation: A virtual world can be a recorded physical world made realistic by capturing the real world with cameras and using computer-vision or SLAM techniques. Triangular meshes describe completely synthetic worlds, texture mapping places real images on synthetic objects, and input queuing handles event processing.

data.text: The virtual world generator is treated as a black box that queues input, maintains an internal virtual reality, and keeps output synchronized with input. It can drive visual, aural, haptic, and other renderers. The needed software support depends on how the world is created: synthetic worlds require computer graphics, while worlds based on real captured images may use SLAM, computer vision, or texture mapping.
points: The virtual world generator is a black-box abstraction of the whole virtual reality software system.
The virtual world generator queues input, maintains an internal reality, and keeps output synchronized with input.
The virtual world generator can drive visual, aural, haptic, and other output renderers.
Synthetic virtual worlds require computer graphics operations for triangular meshes and surface properties.
Virtual reality software may support SLAM, computer vision, and texture mapping of real images onto synthetic objects.

questions.question: What is matched motion in a VR experience?
options: the correspondence between real-world user motion and virtual user motion
the restriction of real-world user motion to a safe physical region
the alignment of real-world obstacle motion and virtual obstacle motion
the conversion of controller input into virtual avatar motion
questions.explanation: Matched motion keeps the user's real-world motions and the corresponding virtual motions aligned. Restricting motion to a safe region describes the matched zone, while controller-driven avatar movement is a form of locomotion.

questions.question: What is the matched zone in a VR setup?
options: a safe real-world region that allows extended virtual movement
a seated controller input that produces avatar movement
a safe virtual region that allows extended real-world movement
a tracked body part that requires matched movement
questions.explanation: The matched zone is the real-world area where physical movement is limited, while movement there can be translated into movement in other parts of the virtual world. It is not a virtual region, a body part, or a controller input.

questions.question: What is an obstacle mismatch in VR?
options: a missing correspondence between a controller command and an avatar action in the matched zone
a missing correspondence between a virtual obstacle and a physical obstacle in the matched zone
a missing correspondence between a user's head motion and the rendered viewpoint in the matched zone
a missing correspondence between a physical location and a virtual location outside the matched zone
questions.explanation: An obstacle mismatch occurs when a virtual obstacle and a physical obstacle do not correspond in the matched zone. Head-motion matching, controller-driven avatar action, and general location mapping are different VR concerns.

questions.question: Why is it useful for VR software to provide several user-locomotion operations?
options: to address cyber sickness
to resolve an obstacle mismatch
to maintain a correct visual viewpoint
to track a user's hand motion
questions.explanation: Different locomotion options are part of VR software because avoiding physical movement can cause cyber sickness, and multiple choices help address it. Correct viewpoint, obstacle matching, and hand tracking are separate matched-motion or rendering needs.

data.text: VR software must keep the user's real movements corresponding to the virtual experience, especially inside the safe matched zone. This includes deciding which body motions to match and preventing physical and virtual obstacles from disagreeing. It must also support user locomotion, where virtual movement does not depend on matched physical movement, while offering choices that may reduce cyber sickness.
points: VR matched motion aligns real and virtual movement, using the safe matched zone as the physical area.
VR obstacle mismatch can occur when physical and virtual obstacles in the matched zone do not correspond.
VR software should support matching head and needed body motions and mapping zone motion to virtual motion.
User locomotion in VR moves the user without matched physical motion, using teleportation, inputs, or vehicles.
Unmatched VR locomotion may increase cyber sickness, so VR software should offer multiple locomotion options.

items.reason: The three required functions of the virtual world generator are reality maintenance, input conversion, and output synchronization, whereas input reception is the separate act of receiving input from devices.

questions.question: Why is virtual reality software needed between a user and virtual reality hardware, rather than the user simply operating the hardware directly?
questions.reference_answer: Virtual reality software is needed because it processes data generated when the user operates input devices. It then sends processed data to output devices, which generate stimuli that are appropriately received by the user's sense organs. This lets the software drive the hardware to create the sensory virtual reality experience.

questions.question: Why must a virtual world generator keep output synchronized with incoming input?
questions.reference_answer: A virtual world generator keeps output synchronized with input to maintain the input-output match that supports an internal reality appearing real to the user. It receives input events from devices such as a head tracker and converts them into outputs for renderers. The renderers then calculate outputs for displays, so the user's actions and the sensory output remain aligned.

questions.question: Why can teleportation and a vehicle metaphor both be useful for user locomotion in virtual reality?
questions.reference_answer: They are useful because user locomotion lets the user move in the virtual world while physical motion in the real world is not matched. Teleportation sends the user to a selected virtual location without any physical movement. A vehicle metaphor lets the user operate a game controller, mouse, or keyboard so the avatar can move while the user remains seated. Such operations may lead to cybersickness.
